gemini_rationale: Although the article draws on empirical fieldwork concerning arsenic-contaminated rural drinking water in Bangladesh (C1=yes, C3=yes), its analytical focus is feminist cultural/political ecology—specifically how societal, spatial, ecological, and bodily factors and ideological constructs of masculinity and femininity produce gendered subjectivities in everyday practices. No legal, regulatory, administrative, tariff/subsidy, formal tenure/documentation, or utility-structure mechanism is examined (C2 narrow=no; E03 wrong exposure), and gendered subjectivity rather than service access is the primary outcome focus (C4=unclear).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2, the study is excluded (E03) because it examines sociocultural gender ideologies, embodied subjectivities, informal norms, and socio-ecological materialities rather than any legal, administrative, regulatory, tenure/documentation, tariff, or utility-governance rule. Under the literal/broad Criterion 2 wording, references to 'water management', 'direct resource use/control/access', and 'prevailing norms and practices' could plausibly encompass informal institutional or community governance arrangements, yielding 'unsure'.

title: Australasian CD34+ quality assurance program and rationale for the clinical utility of the single-platform method for CD34+ cell enumeration
claude_ai_rationale: Quality-assurance program for CD34+ cell enumeration in clinical laboratories; unrelated to water/sanitation access.
gemini_rationale: This record is a clinical hematology laboratory study evaluating quality assurance methods and anticoagulants for CD34+ cell enumeration and white blood cell counts, with no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings because the study is an off-topic clinical hematology laboratory quality assurance evaluation unrelated to water or sanitation service access.
